description:
Check a crypto wallet address: who owns it, which lists name it, and where its funds came from.

A crypto wallet address is checked as an address, never as a name. Pass
the address as written; the chain is detected when omitted.

The answer is the verdict block: `state`, `tier` (block, high, review,
monitor or clear), `score` (0 to 10), `headline`, `main_reason` (a
sentence and its data; `data.kind` is `state_order` when an Israeli
NBCTF seizure or forfeiture order names the address, which is not a
sanctions listing), `owner` with its `evidence` (official_list,
own_publication or bought_label), `list_hits`, `checked` (the chains,
assets, hops and lists covered, and when), `recommended_action`,
`check_id`, `report_url` (the wallet page) and `report_price` (how opening
the full report would be paid).

Each `list_hits` item and `owner` carry `listed_at` (the date the list
names the entry since), `list_ref` (the list's own id of the entry, e.g.
the OFAC uid) and `entry_url` (that entry's official page, e.g. OFAC's
Sanctions List Search). When `entry_url` is null, `source_url` is the
list's own file or notice: say so, never call it the entry's page.

`state`:
- `finished`: the check ran to the end; `checked` says what it covered.
- `pending`: the check is still running (`running: true`). It is not
  finished; collect it with crypto_wallet_result and the `check_id`.
- `incomplete`: not finished. Report it as not finished, never as
  nothing found.
- `unavailable`: no answer could be obtained just now.
- `no_activity`: no transactions were found for the address on the
  chains checked; it may be mistyped, on another chain, or never used.
- `lists_only`: the chain is covered by sanctions lists only, with no
  tracing of funds.
- `invalid`: the address fails its checksum, so it was not checked.

Say what was found and what `checked` covered. The full report is
crypto_wallet_report. `paths_found` is how many paths of funds it holds:
with 0 it states what was read (`checked.read_line`) and shows no money
trail, so never promise one before it is opened.

Examples:
  crypto_wallet_screen("0xabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcd")
  crypto_wallet_screen("0xabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcd", chain="ethereum",
                       customer_ref="case-1042")

address.description: The crypto wallet address to check, exactly as written (for example a TRON address starting with T, an Ethereum address starting with 0x, or a Bitcoin address).

api_key.description: Your Ohmyfin API key (prod-...). Optional here: it can be sent instead as a KEY header or an Authorization: Bearer header. What the tool requires of the key is in its description.

chain.description: Optional chain, e.g. "tron", "ethereum", "bitcoin", "litecoin". Detected from the address when omitted.

customer_ref.description: Optional reference of your own (a customer or case id), kept with the check and returned with it.

name: crypto_wallet_screen
title: Crypto Wallet Check
